specification.problem: Two-qubit Simon problem: given an opaque oracle U_f|x>|y>=|x>|y xor f(x)> with f:{0,1}^2->{0,1}^2 satisfying f(x)=f(x') iff x' in {x, x xor s}, recover the hidden s in {00,01,10,11}. Method: collapse-first ordering with a final Hadamard on the x register, sampled a few times, then GF(2) postprocessing.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Logical 2-qubit Simon on 4 qubits (x: q0,q1; f-register: q2,q3), no ancilla needed for the sampling circuit. Excludes the one-way cluster-state implementation, the photonic experiment, the n-qubit resource analysis, and the swap-test/comparison verification, which is only loosely described in the sketch.

symbols.meaning: input bitstring (x1 x0), q0 is bit 0
input value selected by the output measurement
opaque oracle, one query per sample

equations.label: Oracle action and superposition
equations.description: State after one oracle query on the uniform superposition.
equations.justification: Standard Simon oracle definition with the oracle form given in the task assumptions.

equations.label: Collapse after output measurement
equations.description: Measuring the f-register gives some f value, leaving the x register in the pair state (a single basis state if s=0).
equations.justification: Follows from the 2-to-1 promise; measuring the output register commutes with the final Hadamards on x, so the statistics match the standard circuit.
assumptions: s != 0 for the pair state; x_0 uniform

equations.label: Hadamard readout distribution
equations.description: Distribution of y after H on x. Support is {y: y.s=0 mod 2}. Expected supports: s=11 -> {00,11}; s=01 -> {00,10}; s=10 -> {00,01}; s=00 -> all four.
equations.justification: Standard Simon sampling result; it matches the sketch's expected distributions.
assumptions: Little-endian parsing: y_i = bits[::-1][i], with the string written y1 y0 and s·y = s0 y0 xor s1 y1

equations.label: Linear constraint
equations.description: Each sample gives a linear constraint on s.
equations.justification: Standard Simon postprocessing; the abstract only says the algorithm is solved.

equations.label: Brute-force decoding
equations.latex: \hat s=\begin{cases}s'\neq 0 \text{ such that } y^{(k)}\cdot s'=0\ \forall k & \text{if exactly one such } s' \text{ exists}\\ 00 & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}
equations.description: Test the 3 nonzero candidates against all m samples. If none is consistent, or if more than one is consistent (all y=00 or too few independent samples), report 00 or request more samples. A final check of f(x) versus f(x xor s) can resolve s=0 versus nonzero, at the cost of two more queries.
equations.justification: Postprocessing from the sketch, with the ambiguity rule made explicit.
assumptions: The ambiguity rule is an interpretation of the sketch
s=0 is detected only probabilistically from samples unless the verification step is used

registers.name: x
registers.role: input register; Hadamards then measured to give y

registers.name: f
registers.role: oracle output register; measured to collapse x

registers.name: anc
registers.role: unused in the sampling circuit; reserved for the verification comparison

specification.initial_state: |0000> on q0..q3 (ancilla q4 in |0> if present)

steps.description: Place the opaque U_f once on (q0,q1,q2,q3), with x as controls and q2,q3 as target register.
Measure q2,q3 (or defer; statistics are equal). This collapses x.
Apply H to q0,q1 and measure them into classical bits 0,1. Parse counts with bits[::-1][i] as bit i, and discard the f-register bits from the key if they are measured.
Repeat for m samples (one query per sample). Decode s from the constraints.

specification.measurement: Measure q0,q1 after H into 2 classical bits (little-endian). The q2,q3 measurement is optional and does not change the x statistics.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Collect the distinct y values, then run the brute-force consistency test of eq_5 over s in {01,10,11} with parity y0 s0 xor y1 s1.
assumptions: Choose the 2-qubit instance with qubit cap >= 5
Mid-circuit measurement of the f-register is equivalent to deferred measurement
The final Hadamard on x is the same as in the standard Simon circuit; the sketch's 'collapse-first' ordering does not change the statistics
Swap-test and Hadamard-test ancilla parts of the sketch are not needed for sampling and are not specified here
missing_information: Exact verification circuit (ancilla comparison of f(x) and f(x xor s)) is unspecified
The abstract gives no cluster-state measurement angles, so the one-way implementation is not reconstructed
Number of samples for a target success probability is not specified
